title: Time versus space
objective: Trade memory for speed, and know when that trade is worth it.

sources.title: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed. (MIT Press, 2022): hash tables

simplifies: A set lookup is shown as one step. It usually is, on average, but a set has costs of its own (hashing, extra memory per item) that this count leaves out.

quiz.prompt: You must check 1 million items for duplicates, and memory is plentiful. Which method?

options.explanation: That is about 500 billion comparisons (n(n − 1)/2). Far too slow at this size.

options.text: Remember what you have seen in a set
options.explanation: Right. About 1 million lookups, paid for with memory for up to 1 million items.
They do not: one grows like n², the other like n.

quiz.prompt: What does the set method cost that the pairs method does not?

options.text: Extra memory, up to one entry per item
options.explanation: Right. That memory is the price of finishing in one pass.
It makes far fewer: one lookup per item.
It only reads the list; the set is separate.
